title: बैंककबाट मन्त्री श्रेष्ठको आह्वान- जलवायु तथा भू-विपद्को सामना गर्न क्षेत्रीय सहकार्य र प्रविधि उपयोग गरौं
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौ‌ । ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत तथा सिँचाइ मन्त्री विराज भक्त श्रेष्ठले हिमाली क्षेत्रमा जलवायु परिवर्तनले सिर्जित जटिल विपद् न्यूनीकरणका लागि अन्तरिक्ष प्रविधि, तथ्याङ्क आदानप्रदान र क्षेत्रीय सहकार्यमा जोड दिएका छन्। संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघीय एसिया तथा प्रशान्त क्षेत्रीय आर्थिक र सामाजिक आयोगद्वारा थाइल्याण्डको बैंककमा आयोजित एसिया तथा प्रशान्त क्षेत्रमा दिगो विकासका लागि अन्तरिक्ष अनुप्रयोगसम्बन्धी पाँचौँ मन्त्रीस्तरीय सम्मेलनको उद्घाटन सत्रमा बुधबार विहान मन्तव्य दिँदै मन्त्री श्रेष्ठले जलवायु तथा भू-विपद्को सामना गर्न क्षेत्रीय सहकार्य र प्रविधि उपयोगमा जोड दिएका हुन्। सम्बोधनका क्रममा मन्त्री श्रेष्ठले हालै लङटाङ लिरुङमा हिमपहिरो तथा बुढीगण्डकी क्षेत्रमा पहिरोका कारण भएका ठूला विपद्, जनधनको क्षति र निर्माणाधीन जलविद्युत् आयोजनामा पुगेको असरबारे ध्यानाकर्षण गराए। द्रुत क्षति तथा आवश्यकता आकलनअनुसार विपद्को प्रभाव करिब २.७ अर्ब अमेरिकी डलर बराबर रहेको र पुनःनिर्माणका लागि करिब ४.८ अर्ब डलर आवश्यक पर्ने जानकारी गराए। मन्त्री श्रेष्ठले बैङ्कक मन्त्रिस्तरीय घोषणापत्रको मस्यौदाको स्वागत गर्दै सन् २०२६ देखि २०३० सम्मको तेस्रो चरणमा उपग्रहबाट प्राप्त तथ्याङ्क साझेदारी, पूर्वसूचना प्रणाली र प्राविधिक सहयोगलाई सुदृढ बनाउन अपिल गरे। साथै, हरितगृह ग्यास उत्सर्जनमा नेपालको योगदान नगण्य (०.०१%) रहे पनि सन् २०४५ सम्ममा शून्य कार्बन उत्सर्जन हासिल गर्ने र स्वच्छ ऊर्जा प्रणालीको रक्षा गर्ने नेपालको प्रतिबद्धता दोहोर्याए। सम्मेलनका अवसरमा विहीबार २९ अक्टोबरमा नेपाल र संयुक्त राष्ट्रसङ्घीय ईएससीएपीको संयुक्त आयोजनामा ‘सगरमाथादेखि सागरसम्म: भोटेकोशी-त्रिशूली विपद्का पाठहरू’ विषयक क्षेत्रीय संवाद समेत सञ्चालन हुन गइरहेको पनि जानकारी गराउँदै सहभागी हुन अनुरोध गरे। सम्बोधनको पूर्ण पाठ : नेपालको तर्फबाट यस सम्मेलनलाई सम्बोधन गर्न पाउँदा म अत्यन्तै सम्मानित महसुस गर्दछु। अन्तरिक्ष अनुप्रयोगहरूमा क्षेत्रीय सहयोगलाई सुदृढ बनाउन हामीलाई एकै ठाउँमा ल्याउनुभएकोमा म ESCAP र रोयल थाई सरकारलाई धन्यवाद दिन्छु। नेपालका लागि यो छलफलको मानिसहरूको जीवनसँग प्रत्यक्ष र तत्काल सम्बन्ध छ। यसले हिमाली समुदायको सुरक्षा, जलस्रोतको दिगो उपयोग र वर्षौंसम्मको कडा परिश्रमबाट निर्माण भएको विकासको रक्षा गर्ने विषयसँग सरोकार राख्छ। गत २६ अगस्टमा लङटाङ लिरुङको उच्च भागमा चट्टान र हिमनदीको बरफ फुटेर गयो। यसले भोटेकोशी र त्रिशूली नदीहरूमा पानी, बरफ र लेदोको भीषण बहाव ल्यायो। यस घटनामा १,४०० भन्दा बढी मानिसहरूले ज्यान गुमाए भने ५,००० भन्दा बढी अझै बेपत्ता छन्। बस्ती, सडक, पुल, सीमा नाका र जलविद्युत् आयोजनाहरू ध्वस्त भए। त्यसपछि ११ अक्टोबरमा बुढीगण्डकीमा पहिरोले नदी थुनिएर फुट्दा निर्माणाधीन एक प्रमुख जलविद्युत् आयोजनामा क्षति पुर्यायो। द्रुत क्षति तथा आवश्यकता आकलन (Rapid Damage and Need Assessment) ले विपद्को कुल प्रभाव करिब २.७ अर्ब अमेरिकी डलर बराबर रहेको र पुनःप्राप्ति तथा पुनर्मार्माणका लागि करिब ४.८ अर्ब डलर आवश्यक पर्ने अनुमान गरेको छ। यी घटनाहरूले हामीले सामना गरिरहेका जोखिमहरूको जटिलतालाई दर्शाउँछन्। सुक्खा हिमपहिरोले नदी थुनेर अस्थायी ताल बनाउन सक्छ र धेरै तल्लो तटीय क्षेत्रमा बाढी ल्याउन सक्छ। केवल वर्षाको पूर्वानुमानले मात्र यो सम्पूर्ण श्रृंखलालाई समेट्न सक्दैन। उच्च हिमालयमा उत्पन्न भएको विपद् केही घण्टामै सयौँ किलोमिटर टाढा, विभिन्न जिल्ला र सीमापारिसम्म पुग्न सक्छ। हाम्रा हिमालहरूको यो नयाँ यथार्थ हो। जलवायु परिवर्तनले हाम्रो संवेदनशील हिमाली पारिस्थितिकी प्रणालीमा निरन्तर दबाब सिर्जना गरिरहेको छ। प्रत्येक घटनाको विस्तृत वैज्ञानिक अनुसन्धान आवश्यक भए तापनि, अनुगमन र तयारीलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता स्पष्ट छ। जकार्ता मन्त्रिस्तरीय घोषणापत्रले हाम्रो क्षेत्रलाई एउटा साझा दिशा दिएको छ: मजबुत साझेदारी, डिजिटल प्रविधिको अझ राम्रो प्रयोग, सुधारिएको डाटा व्यवस्थापन, र यी सूचनाहरू प्रयोग गर्ने मानिसहरूसँग नजिकको संलग्नता। भोटेकोशी विपद्को कारण पत्ता लगाउन तत्काल उपग्रहका तस्बिरहरू र प्राविधिक जानकारी उपलब्ध गराएकोमा म ESCAP लाई हार्दिक धन्यवाद दिन्छु। सहायताका लागि म मित्र राष्ट्रहरू, क्षेत्रीय संस्थाहरू र विकास साझेदारहरूलाई पनि धन्यवाद दिन्छु। ESCAP का प्रतिवेदनहरूमा उल्लेख गरिए अनुसार उपग्रहका तस्बिरहरू र विपद् सम्बन्धी जानकारी साझा गर्ने कार्य, असल अभ्यासहरू, तथा विपद् विश्लेषणका लागि SatGPT प्रयोग गर्ने तालिम सराहनीय छन्। यी उपलब्धिहरूले क्षेत्रीय प्रतिबद्धताहरू कसरी उपयोगी सेवामा परिणत हुन सक्छन् भन्ने देखाउँछन्। अब हामीले यसको पहुँच विस्तार गर्नुपर्छ र यिनको प्रयोगका लागि राष्ट्रिय क्षमता सुदृढ गर्नुपर्छ। नेपाल यस सम्मेलन समक्ष प्रस्तुत ब्याङ्कक मन्त्रिस्तरीय घोषणापत्रको मस्यौदाको स्वागत गर्दछ। यसले डाटा साझेदारी, अनुकूल प्रणाली, व्यावहारिक डिजिटल उपकरण र प्राविधिक सहायतामा दिएको जोडले सन् २०२६ देखि २०३० सम्मको तेस्रो चरणमा सहयोगलाई सुदृढ बनाउन सक्छ। सबैका लागि पूर्वसूचना (Early Warnings for All) र दुर्गम तथा हिमाली क्षेत्रमा स्याटेलाइट कनेक्टिभिटीका लागि यसको समर्थन नेपालका लागि विशेष सान्दर्भिक छ। हाम्रा लागि कार्यान्वयनको अर्थ हिमनदी, हिमताल र अस्थिर ढलानहरूको नियमित अनुगमन; माथिल्लो तटीय क्षेत्रका जोखिमबारे समयमै सूचना आदानप्रदान; र समुदायसम्म स्पष्ट मार्गनिर्देशनसहितका चेतावनीहरू पुग्नु हो। हामी क्षेत्रीय साझेदारहरूलाई उपग्रह अवलोकनलाई जमिनको मापन र स्थानीय ज्ञानसँग संयोजन गर्दै, शृङ्खलाबद्ध (cascading) हिमाली जोखिमहरूमा संयुक्त कार्यक्रमहरू विकास गर्न प्रोत्साहन गर्दछौँ। अन्तरिक्ष अनुप्रयोगहरूले सुरक्षित जलविद्युत् विकास, सिँचाइ आयोजना र जलाधार व्यवस्थापनलाई पनि मार्गदर्शन गर्न सक्छन्। नेपालको पूर्ण रूपमा स्वच्छ ऊर्जा प्रणालीलाई कायम राख्ने जलविद्युत् विकास, व्यापक ऊर्जा पूर्वाधार र लगानीको सुरक्षा तथा संरक्षण गर्न हामी पूर्ण रूपमा प्रतिबद्ध छौँ। नेपाल आफ्नो राष्ट्रिय अनुकूलन योजना (२०२१-२०५०), तेस्रो राष्ट्रिय निर्धारित योगदान (NDC), र सन् २०४५ सम्ममा शून्य कार्बन उत्सर्जन (net-zero) हासिल गर्ने लक्ष्यप्रति प्रतिबद्ध छ। विश्वव्यापी हरितगृह ग्यास उत्सर्जनमा हाम्रो नगण्य ०.०१% योगदान भए तापनि, हामी स्वच्छ ऊर्जा, जलवायु उत्थानशीलता र व्यावहारिक क्षेत्रीय सहयोगका लागि प्रतिबद्ध छौँ। नेपाल बहु-जोखिम र जलवायु परिवर्तनका प्रभावहरू सम्बन्धी अनुसन्धान र सिकाइका लागि क्षेत्रीय केन्द्र (hub) को रूपमा सेवा गर्न तयार छ, साथै एसिया प्रशान्त क्षेत्रभरि बहु-जोखिम जोखिम न्यूनीकरण र व्यवस्थापनमा उत्तम अभ्यासहरू साझा गर्न चाहन्छ। नेपाल र UN ESCAP ले संयुक्त रूपमा भोलि २९ अक्टोबर बिहान १०:०० बजेदेखि दिउँसो १:०० बजेसम्म सम्मेलन कक्ष ४ मा “सगरमाथादेखि सागरसम्म: एसिया र प्रशान्त क्षेत्रमा शृङ्खलाबद्ध जोखिमहरू विरुद्ध उत्थानशीलता सुदृढ गर्न नेपालको भोटेकोशी-त्रिशूली विपद्का पाठहरू” शीर्षकमा क्षेत्रीय संवाद आयोजना गर्दैछन्। यस कार्यक्रमको उद्देश्य जलवायु, हिमनदी, भू-भौतिकीय र तटीय जोखिमहरू कसरी जोडिन्छन् र “हिमालदेखि समुद्रसम्म” क्षेत्र र सीमापारि विपद्हरू निम्त्याउँछन् भन्ने बुझाइमा सुधार ल्याउनु हो। यसले उपग्रह अवलोकन, भू-स्थानिक विश्लेषण, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (AI) र युवा नेतृत्वको नवप्रवर्तनले विपद् तयारीलाई कसरी सुदृढ बनाउन सक्छ भन्ने कुरालाई उजागर गर्दै डाटा साझेदारी, अनुगमन, पूर्व चेतावनी र जोखिम-सूचित योजनामा क्षेत्रीय सहयोगलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्नेछ। म सबै प्रतिनिधिमण्डलहरूलाई सहभागी हुन हार्दिक निमन्त्रणा गर्दछु। आउनुहोस्, ब्याङ्कक घोषणापत्रमार्फत जकार्ताको भावनालाई अगाडि बढाऔँ, जसले देशहरूलाई जोखिम बुझ्न, विकासको रक्षा गर्न र मानिसहरूको जीवन रक्षा गर्न मद्दत गर्नेछ। धन्यवाद। Kathmandu. Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has emphasized on space technology, data exchange and regional cooperation to mitigate complex disasters caused by climate change in the Himalayan region. Speaking at the opening session of the Fifth Ministerial Conference on Space Applications for Sustainable Development in Asia and the Pacific organized by the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific in Bangkok, Thailand, on Wednesday morning, Minister Shrestha emphasized regional cooperation and use of technology to combat climate and geo-disasters. During his address, Minister Shrestha drew attention to the recent major disasters caused by avalanches in Langtang Lirung and landslides in the Budhi Gandaki region, the loss of life and property, and the impact on the under-construction hydropower projects. According to the rapid damage and needs assessment, the impact of the disaster is estimated at approximately US$2.7 billion and approximately US$4.8 billion is required for reconstruction. Minister Shrestha welcomed the draft of the Bangkok Ministerial Declaration and appealed for strengthening satellite data sharing, early warning systems, and technical cooperation in the third phase from 2026 to 2030. He also reiterated Nepal's commitment to achieving zero carbon emissions by 2045 and protecting a clean energy system, even though Nepal's contribution to greenhouse gas emissions is negligible (0.01%). On the occasion of the conference, he also informed that a regional dialogue on the topic 'From Everest to the Sea: Lessons from the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disaster' will be held on Thursday, October 29, jointly organized by Nepal and the United Nations ESCAP, and requested participation. Full text of the address: I feel deeply honored to address this conference on behalf of Nepal. I thank ESCAP and the Royal Thai Government for bringing us together to strengthen regional cooperation in space applications. For Nepal, this discussion has a direct and immediate connection to people's lives. It concerns the security of Himalayan communities, the sustainable use of water resources, and the preservation of development built through years of hard work. On August 26, a rock and glacier burst in the upper reaches of the Langtang Lirung. This unleashed a torrent of water, ice, and mud into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers. More than 1,400 people lost their lives in the incident, while more than 5,000 are still missing. Settlements, roads, bridges, border posts, and hydroelectric projects were destroyed. Then, on October 11, a landslide in the Budhi Gandaki blocked the river and burst, damaging a major hydroelectric project under construction. The Rapid Damage and Need Assessment estimates the total impact of the disaster to be approximately $2.7 billion, with approximately $4.8 billion needed for recovery and reconstruction. These events illustrate the complexity of the risks we face. Dry avalanches can block rivers, creating temporary lakes and flooding many low-lying coastal areas. Rainfall forecasts alone cannot cover the full range of these hazards. A disaster originating in the high Himalayas can spread hundreds of kilometers away, to different districts and across borders, within hours. This is the new reality of our mountains. Climate change is placing continued pressure on our sensitive mountain ecosystems. While detailed scientific investigation of each event is necessary, the need to promote monitoring and preparedness is clear. The Jakarta Ministerial Declaration has given our region a common direction: stronger partnerships, better use of digital technologies, improved data management, and closer engagement with the people who use this information. I sincerely thank ESCAP for providing the satellite imagery and technical information needed to quickly identify the causes of the Bhotekoshi disaster. I also thank friendly countries, regional organizations, and development partners for their support. The sharing of satellite imagery and disaster information, good practices, and training in using SatGPT for disaster analysis, as noted in ESCAP reports, are commendable. These achievements demonstrate how regional commitments can be translated into useful services. We now need to expand its reach and strengthen national capacity for its use. Nepal welcomes the draft Bangkok Ministerial Declaration presented to this conference. It can strengthen cooperation in the third phase from 2026 to 2030, with its emphasis on data sharing, adaptive systems, practical digital tools, and technical assistance. Early Warnings for All and its support for satellite connectivity in remote and mountainous areas are particularly relevant for Nepal. Nepal is committed to its National Adaptation Plan (2021-2050), the third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), and the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2045. Nepal is poised to serve as a regional hub for research and learning on multi-hazards and climate change impacts, as well as share best practices in multi-hazard risk reduction and management across the Asia Pacific region. The event aims to improve understanding of how climate, glacial, geophysical and coastal hazards are interconnected and lead to regional and transboundary disasters “from mountains to sea”. It will promote regional cooperation in data sharing, monitoring, early warning and risk-informed planning, highlighting how satellite observations, geospatial analysis, artificial intelligence (AI) and youth-led innovation can strengthen disaster preparedness. I cordially invite all delegations to participate. Let us take forward the spirit of Jakarta through the Bangkok Declaration, which will help countries understand risks, protect development, and save lives. Thank you.

According to the rapid damage and needs assessment, the impact of the disaster is estimated at approximately US$2.7 billion and approximately US$4.8 billion is required for reconstruction. Minister Shrestha welcomed the draft of the Bangkok Ministerial Declaration and appealed for strengthening satellite data sharing, early warning systems, and technical cooperation in the third phase from 2026 to 2030. He also reiterated Nepal's commitment to achieving zero carbon emissions by 2045 and protecting a clean energy system, even though Nepal's contribution to greenhouse gas emissions is negligible (0.01%). On the occasion of the conference, he also informed that a regional dialogue on the topic 'From Everest to the Sea: Lessons from the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disaster' will be held on Thursday, October 29, jointly organized by Nepal and the United Nations ESCAP, and requested participation. Full text of the address: I feel deeply honored to address this conference on behalf of Nepal. I thank ESCAP and the Royal Thai Government for bringing us together to strengthen regional cooperation in space applications. For Nepal, this discussion has a direct and immediate connection to people's lives. It concerns the security of Himalayan communities, the sustainable use of water resources, and the preservation of development built through years of hard work. On August 26, a rock and glacier burst in the upper reaches of the Langtang Lirung. This unleashed a torrent of water, ice, and mud into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers. More than 1,400 people lost their lives in the incident, while more than 5,000 are still missing. Settlements, roads, bridges, border posts, and hydroelectric projects were destroyed. Then, on October 11, a landslide in the Budhi Gandaki blocked the river and burst, damaging a major hydroelectric project under construction. The Rapid Damage and Need Assessment estimates the total impact of the disaster to be approximately $2.7 billion, with approximately $4.8 billion needed for recovery and reconstruction. These events illustrate the complexity of the risks we face. Dry avalanches can block rivers, creating temporary lakes and flooding many low-lying coastal areas. Rainfall forecasts alone cannot cover the full range of these hazards. A disaster originating in the high Himalayas can spread hundreds of kilometers away, to different districts and across borders, within hours. This is the new reality of our mountains. Climate change is placing continued pressure on our sensitive mountain ecosystems. While detailed scientific investigation of each event is necessary, the need to promote monitoring and preparedness is clear. The Jakarta Ministerial Declaration has given our region a common direction: stronger partnerships, better use of digital technologies, improved data management, and closer engagement with the people who use this information. I sincerely thank ESCAP for providing the satellite imagery and technical information needed to quickly identify the causes of the Bhotekoshi disaster. I also thank friendly countries, regional organizations, and development partners for their support. The sharing of satellite imagery and disaster information, good practices, and training in using SatGPT for disaster analysis, as noted in ESCAP reports, are commendable. These achievements demonstrate how regional commitments can be translated into useful services. We now need to expand its reach and strengthen national capacity for its use. Nepal welcomes the draft Bangkok Ministerial Declaration presented to this conference. It can strengthen cooperation in the third phase from 2026 to 2030, with its emphasis on data sharing, adaptive systems, practical digital tools, and technical assistance. Early Warnings for All and its support for satellite connectivity in remote and mountainous areas are particularly relevant for Nepal. For us, implementation means regular monitoring of glaciers, glacial lakes, and unstable slopes; timely information sharing on risks in the upper coastal areas; and reaching communities with clear guidance on warnings. We encourage regional partners to develop joint programs on cascading mountain hazards, combining satellite observations with ground measurements and local knowledge. Space applications can also guide safe hydropower development, irrigation projects, and watershed management. We are fully committed to protecting and preserving hydropower development, comprehensive energy infrastructure, and investments that will sustain Nepal's completely clean energy system. Nepal is committed to its National Adaptation Plan (2021-2050), the third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), and the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2045. Despite our negligible contribution of 0.01% to global greenhouse gas emissions, we are committed to clean energy, climate resilience, and practical regional cooperation. Nepal is poised to serve as a regional hub for research and learning on multi-hazards and climate change impacts, as well as share best practices in multi-hazard risk reduction and management across the Asia Pacific region. Nepal and UN ESCAP are jointly organizing a regional dialogue titled “From Everest to the Ocean: Lessons from Nepal’s Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disasters to Strengthen Resilience against Chaining Hazards in Asia and the Pacific” on October 29 from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM in Conference Room 4. The event aims to improve understanding of how climate, glacial, geophysical and coastal hazards are interconnected and lead to regional and transboundary disasters “from mountains to sea”. It will promote regional cooperation in data sharing, monitoring, early warning and risk-informed planning, highlighting how satellite observations, geospatial analysis, artificial intelligence (AI) and youth-led innovation can strengthen disaster preparedness. I cordially invite all delegations to participate. Let us take forward the spirit of Jakarta through the Bangkok Declaration, which will help countries understand risks, protect development, and save lives. Thank you.

Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has emphasized on space technology, data exchange and regional cooperation to mitigate complex disasters caused by climate change in the Himalayan region. Speaking at the opening session of the Fifth Ministerial Conference on Space Applications for Sustainable Development in Asia and the Pacific organized by the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific in Bangkok, Thailand, on Wednesday morning, Minister Shrestha emphasized regional cooperation and use of technology to combat climate and geo-disasters. During his address, Minister Shrestha drew attention to the recent major disasters caused by avalanches in Langtang Lirung and landslides in the Budhi Gandaki region, the loss of life and property, and the impact on the under-construction hydropower projects. According to the rapid damage and needs assessment, the impact of the disaster is estimated at approximately US$2.7 billion and approximately US$4.8 billion is required for reconstruction. Minister Shrestha welcomed the draft of the Bangkok Ministerial Declaration and appealed for strengthening satellite data sharing, early warning systems, and technical cooperation in the third phase from 2026 to 2030. He also reiterated Nepal's commitment to achieving zero carbon emissions by 2045 and protecting a clean energy system, even though Nepal's contribution to greenhouse gas emissions is negligible (0.01%). On the occasion of the conference, he also informed that a regional dialogue on the topic 'From Everest to the Sea: Lessons from the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disaster' will be held on Thursday, October 29, jointly organized by Nepal and the United Nations ESCAP, and requested participation. Full text of the address: I feel deeply honored to address this conference on behalf of Nepal. I thank ESCAP and the Royal Thai Government for bringing us together to strengthen regional cooperation in space applications. For Nepal, this discussion has a direct and immediate connection to people's lives. It concerns the security of Himalayan communities, the sustainable use of water resources, and the preservation of development built through years of hard work. On August 26, a rock and glacier burst in the upper reaches of the Langtang Lirung. This unleashed a torrent of water, ice, and mud into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers. More than 1,400 people lost their lives in the incident, while more than 5,000 are still missing. Settlements, roads, bridges, border posts, and hydroelectric projects were destroyed. Then, on October 11, a landslide in the Budhi Gandaki blocked the river and burst, damaging a major hydroelectric project under construction. The Rapid Damage and Need Assessment estimates the total impact of the disaster to be approximately $2.7 billion, with approximately $4.8 billion needed for recovery and reconstruction. These events illustrate the complexity of the risks we face. Dry avalanches can block rivers, creating temporary lakes and flooding many low-lying coastal areas. Rainfall forecasts alone cannot cover the full range of these hazards. A disaster originating in the high Himalayas can spread hundreds of kilometers away, to different districts and across borders, within hours. This is the new reality of our mountains. Climate change is placing continued pressure on our sensitive mountain ecosystems. While detailed scientific investigation of each event is necessary, the need to promote monitoring and preparedness is clear. The Jakarta Ministerial Declaration has given our region a common direction: stronger partnerships, better use of digital technologies, improved data management, and closer engagement with the people who use this information. I sincerely thank ESCAP for providing the satellite imagery and technical information needed to quickly identify the causes of the Bhotekoshi disaster. I also thank friendly countries, regional organizations, and development partners for their support. The sharing of satellite imagery and disaster information, good practices, and training in using SatGPT for disaster analysis, as noted in ESCAP reports, are commendable. These achievements demonstrate how regional commitments can be translated into useful services. We now need to expand its reach and strengthen national capacity for its use. Nepal welcomes the draft Bangkok Ministerial Declaration presented to this conference. It can strengthen cooperation in the third phase from 2026 to 2030, with its emphasis on data sharing, adaptive systems, practical digital tools, and technical assistance. Early Warnings for All and its support for satellite connectivity in remote and mountainous areas are particularly relevant for Nepal. For us, implementation means regular monitoring of glaciers, glacial lakes, and unstable slopes; timely information sharing on risks in the upper coastal areas; and reaching communities with clear guidance on warnings. We encourage regional partners to develop joint programs on cascading mountain hazards, combining satellite observations with ground measurements and local knowledge. Space applications can also guide safe hydropower development, irrigation projects, and watershed management. We are fully committed to protecting and preserving hydropower development, comprehensive energy infrastructure, and investments that will sustain Nepal's completely clean energy system. Nepal is committed to its National Adaptation Plan (2021-2050), the third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), and the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2045. Despite our negligible contribution of 0.01% to global greenhouse gas emissions, we are committed to clean energy, climate resilience, and practical regional cooperation. Nepal is poised to serve as a regional hub for research and learning on multi-hazards and climate change impacts, as well as share best practices in multi-hazard risk reduction and management across the Asia Pacific region. Nepal and UN ESCAP are jointly organizing a regional dialogue titled “From Everest to the Ocean: Lessons from Nepal’s Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disasters to Strengthen Resilience against Chaining Hazards in Asia and the Pacific” on October 29 from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM in Conference Room 4. The event aims to improve understanding of how climate, glacial, geophysical and coastal hazards are interconnected and lead to regional and transboundary disasters “from mountains to sea”. It will promote regional cooperation in data sharing, monitoring, early warning and risk-informed planning, highlighting how satellite observations, geospatial analysis, artificial intelligence (AI) and youth-led innovation can strengthen disaster preparedness. I cordially invite all delegations to participate. Let us take forward the spirit of Jakarta through the Bangkok Declaration, which will help countries understand risks, protect development, and save lives. Thank you.

Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has emphasized on space technology, data exchange and regional cooperation to mitigate complex disasters caused by climate change in the Himalayan region. Speaking at the opening session of the Fifth Ministerial Conference on Space Applications for Sustainable Development in Asia and the Pacific organized by the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific in Bangkok, Thailand, on Wednesday morning, Minister Shrestha emphasized regional cooperation and use of technology to combat climate and geo-disasters. During his address, Minister Shrestha drew attention to the recent major disasters caused by avalanches in Langtang Lirung and landslides in the Budhi Gandaki region, the loss of life and property, and the impact on the under-construction hydropower projects. According to the rapid damage and needs assessment, the impact of the disaster is estimated at approximately US$2.7 billion and approximately US$4.8 billion is required for reconstruction. Minister Shrestha welcomed the draft of the Bangkok Ministerial Declaration and appealed for strengthening satellite data sharing, early warning systems, and technical cooperation in the third phase from 2026 to 2030. He also reiterated Nepal's commitment to achieving zero carbon emissions by 2045 and protecting a clean energy system, even though Nepal's contribution to greenhouse gas emissions is negligible (0.01%). On the occasion of the conference, he also informed that a regional dialogue on the topic 'From Everest to the Sea: Lessons from the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disaster' will be held on Thursday, October 29, jointly organized by Nepal and the United Nations ESCAP, and requested participation. Full text of the address: I feel deeply honored to address this conference on behalf of Nepal. I thank ESCAP and the Royal Thai Government for bringing us together to strengthen regional cooperation in space applications. For Nepal, this discussion has a direct and immediate connection to people's lives. It concerns the security of Himalayan communities, the sustainable use of water resources, and the preservation of development built through years of hard work. On August 26, a rock and glacier burst in the upper reaches of the Langtang Lirung. This unleashed a torrent of water, ice, and mud into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers. More than 1,400 people lost their lives in the incident, while more than 5,000 are still missing. Settlements, roads, bridges, border posts, and hydroelectric projects were destroyed. Then, on October 11, a landslide in the Budhi Gandaki blocked the river and burst, damaging a major hydroelectric project under construction. The Rapid Damage and Need Assessment estimates the total impact of the disaster to be approximately $2.7 billion, with approximately $4.8 billion needed for recovery and reconstruction. These events illustrate the complexity of the risks we face. Dry avalanches can block rivers, creating temporary lakes and flooding many low-lying coastal areas. Rainfall forecasts alone cannot cover the full range of these hazards. A disaster originating in the high Himalayas can spread hundreds of kilometers away, to different districts and across borders, within hours. This is the new reality of our mountains. Climate change is placing continued pressure on our sensitive mountain ecosystems. While detailed scientific investigation of each event is necessary, the need to promote monitoring and preparedness is clear. The Jakarta Ministerial Declaration has given our region a common direction: stronger partnerships, better use of digital technologies, improved data management, and closer engagement with the people who use this information. I sincerely thank ESCAP for providing the satellite imagery and technical information needed to quickly identify the causes of the Bhotekoshi disaster. I also thank friendly countries, regional organizations, and development partners for their support. The sharing of satellite imagery and disaster information, good practices, and training in using SatGPT for disaster analysis, as noted in ESCAP reports, are commendable. These achievements demonstrate how regional commitments can be translated into useful services. We now need to expand its reach and strengthen national capacity for its use. Nepal welcomes the draft Bangkok Ministerial Declaration presented to this conference. It can strengthen cooperation in the third phase from 2026 to 2030, with its emphasis on data sharing, adaptive systems, practical digital tools, and technical assistance. Early Warnings for All and its support for satellite connectivity in remote and mountainous areas are particularly relevant for Nepal. For us, implementation means regular monitoring of glaciers, glacial lakes, and unstable slopes; timely information sharing on risks in the upper coastal areas; and reaching communities with clear guidance on warnings. We encourage regional partners to develop joint programs on cascading mountain hazards, combining satellite observations with ground measurements and local knowledge. Space applications can also guide safe hydropower development, irrigation projects, and watershed management. We are fully committed to protecting and preserving hydropower development, comprehensive energy infrastructure, and investments that will sustain Nepal's completely clean energy system. Nepal is committed to its National Adaptation Plan (2021-2050), the third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), and the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2045. Despite our negligible contribution of 0.01% to global greenhouse gas emissions, we are committed to clean energy, climate resilience, and practical regional cooperation. Nepal is poised to serve as a regional hub for research and learning on multi-hazards and climate change impacts, as well as share best practices in multi-hazard risk reduction and management across the Asia Pacific region. Nepal and UN ESCAP are jointly organizing a regional dialogue titled “From Everest to the Ocean: Lessons from Nepal’s Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disasters to Strengthen Resilience against Chaining Hazards in Asia and the Pacific” on October 29 from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM in Conference Room 4. The event aims to improve understanding of how climate, glacial, geophysical and coastal hazards are interconnected and lead to regional and transboundary disasters “from mountains to sea”. It will promote regional cooperation in data sharing, monitoring, early warning and risk-informed planning, highlighting how satellite observations, geospatial analysis, artificial intelligence (AI) and youth-led innovation can strengthen disaster preparedness. I cordially invite all delegations to participate. Let us take forward the spirit of Jakarta through the Bangkok Declaration, which will help countries understand risks, protect development, and save lives. Thank you.

गर्दै, शृङ्खलाबद्ध (cascading) हिमाली जोखिमहरूमा संयुक्त कार्यक्रमहरू विकास गर्न प्रोत्साहन गर्दछौँ। अन्तरिक्ष अनुप्रयोगहरूले सुरक्षित जलविद्युत् विकास, सिँचाइ आयोजना र जलाधार व्यवस्थापनलाई पनि मार्गदर्शन गर्न सक्छन्। नेपालको पूर्ण रूपमा स्वच्छ ऊर्जा प्रणालीलाई कायम राख्ने जलविद्युत् विकास, व्यापक ऊर्जा पूर्वाधार र लगानीको सुरक्षा तथा संरक्षण गर्न हामी पूर्ण रूपमा प्रतिबद्ध छौँ। नेपाल आफ्नो राष्ट्रिय अनुकूलन योजना (२०२१-२०५०), तेस्रो राष्ट्रिय निर्धारित योगदान (NDC), र सन् २०४५ सम्ममा शून्य कार्बन उत्सर्जन (net-zero) हासिल गर्ने लक्ष्यप्रति प्रतिबद्ध छ। विश्वव्यापी हरितगृह ग्यास उत्सर्जनमा हाम्रो नगण्य ०.०१% योगदान भए तापनि, हामी स्वच्छ ऊर्जा, जलवायु उत्थानशीलता र व्यावहारिक क्षेत्रीय सहयोगका लागि प्रतिबद्ध छौँ। नेपाल बहु-जोखिम र जलवायु परिवर्तनका प्रभावहरू सम्बन्धी अनुसन्धान र सिकाइका लागि क्षेत्रीय केन्द्र (hub) को रूपमा सेवा गर्न तयार छ, साथै एसिया प्रशान्त क्षेत्रभरि बहु-जोखिम जोखिम न्यूनीकरण र व्यवस्थापनमा उत्तम अभ्यासहरू साझा गर्न चाहन्छ। नेपाल र UN ESCAP ले संयुक्त रूपमा भोलि २९ अक्टोबर बिहान १०:०० बजेदेखि दिउँसो १:०० बजेसम्म सम्मेलन कक्ष ४ मा “सगरमाथादेखि सागरसम्म: एसिया र प्रशान्त क्षेत्रमा शृङ्खलाबद्ध जोखिमहरू विरुद्ध उत्थानशीलता सुदृढ गर्न नेपालको भोटेकोशी-त्रिशूली विपद्का पाठहरू” शीर्षकमा क्षेत्रीय संवाद आयोजना गर्दैछन्। यस कार्यक्रमको उद्देश्य जलवायु, हिमनदी, भू-भौतिकीय र तटीय जोखिमहरू कसरी जोडिन्छन् र “हिमालदेखि समुद्रसम्म” क्षेत्र र सीमापारि विपद्हरू निम्त्याउँछन् भन्ने बुझाइमा सुधार ल्याउनु हो। यसले उपग्रह अवलोकन, भू-स्थानिक विश्लेषण, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (AI) र युवा नेतृत्वको नवप्रवर्तनले विपद् तयारीलाई कसरी सुदृढ बनाउन सक्छ भन्ने कुरालाई उजागर गर्दै डाटा साझेदारी, अनुगमन, पूर्व चेतावनी र जोखिम-सूचित योजनामा क्षेत्रीय सहयोगलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्नेछ। म सबै प्रतिनिधिमण्डलहरूलाई सहभागी हुन हार्दिक निमन्त्रणा गर्दछु। आउनुहोस्, ब्याङ्कक घोषणापत्रमार्फत जकार्ताको भावनालाई अगाडि बढाऔँ, जसले देशहरूलाई जोखिम बुझ्न, विकासको रक्षा गर्न र मानिसहरूको जीवन रक्षा गर्न मद्दत गर्नेछ। धन्यवाद।

काठमाडौ‌ । ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत तथा सिँचाइ मन्त्री विराज भक्त श्रेष्ठले हिमाली क्षेत्रमा जलवायु परिवर्तनले सिर्जित जटिल विपद् न्यूनीकरणका लागि अन्तरिक्ष प्रविधि, तथ्याङ्क आदानप्रदान र क्षेत्रीय सहकार्यमा जोड दिएका छन्।

संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघीय एसिया तथा प्रशान्त क्षेत्रीय आर्थिक र सामाजिक आयोगद्वारा थाइल्याण्डको बैंककमा आयोजित एसिया तथा प्रशान्त क्षेत्रमा दिगो विकासका लागि अन्तरिक्ष अनुप्रयोगसम्बन्धी पाँचौँ मन्त्रीस्तरीय सम्मेलनको उद्घाटन सत्रमा बुधबार विहान मन्तव्य दिँदै मन्त्री श्रेष्ठले जलवायु तथा भू-विपद्को सामना गर्न क्षेत्रीय सहकार्य र प्रविधि उपयोगमा जोड दिएका हुन्।

सम्बोधनका क्रममा मन्त्री श्रेष्ठले हालै लङटाङ लिरुङमा हिमपहिरो तथा बुढीगण्डकी क्षेत्रमा पहिरोका कारण भएका ठूला विपद्, जनधनको क्षति र निर्माणाधीन जलविद्युत् आयोजनामा पुगेको असरबारे ध्यानाकर्षण गराए।

द्रुत क्षति तथा आवश्यकता आकलनअनुसार विपद्को प्रभाव करिब २.७ अर्ब अमेरिकी डलर बराबर रहेको र पुनःनिर्माणका लागि करिब ४.८ अर्ब डलर आवश्यक पर्ने जानकारी गराए।

मन्त्री श्रेष्ठले बैङ्कक मन्त्रिस्तरीय घोषणापत्रको मस्यौदाको स्वागत गर्दै सन् २०२६ देखि २०३० सम्मको तेस्रो चरणमा उपग्रहबाट प्राप्त तथ्याङ्क साझेदारी, पूर्वसूचना प्रणाली र प्राविधिक सहयोगलाई सुदृढ बनाउन अपिल गरे।

साथै, हरितगृह ग्यास उत्सर्जनमा नेपालको योगदान नगण्य (०.०१%) रहे पनि सन् २०४५ सम्ममा शून्य कार्बन उत्सर्जन हासिल गर्ने र स्वच्छ ऊर्जा प्रणालीको रक्षा गर्ने नेपालको प्रतिबद्धता दोहोर्याए।

सम्मेलनका अवसरमा विहीबार २९ अक्टोबरमा नेपाल र संयुक्त राष्ट्रसङ्घीय ईएससीएपीको संयुक्त आयोजनामा ‘सगरमाथादेखि सागरसम्म: भोटेकोशी-त्रिशूली विपद्का पाठहरू’ विषयक क्षेत्रीय संवाद समेत सञ्चालन हुन गइरहेको पनि जानकारी गराउँदै सहभागी हुन अनुरोध गरे।

सम्बोधनको पूर्ण पाठ :

नेपालको तर्फबाट यस सम्मेलनलाई सम्बोधन गर्न पाउँदा म अत्यन्तै सम्मानित महसुस गर्दछु। अन्तरिक्ष अनुप्रयोगहरूमा क्षेत्रीय सहयोगलाई सुदृढ बनाउन हामीलाई एकै ठाउँमा ल्याउनुभएकोमा म ESCAP र रोयल थाई सरकारलाई धन्यवाद दिन्छु। नेपालका लागि यो छलफलको मानिसहरूको जीवनसँग प्रत्यक्ष र तत्काल सम्बन्ध छ। यसले हिमाली समुदायको सुरक्षा, जलस्रोतको दिगो उपयोग र वर्षौंसम्मको कडा परिश्रमबाट निर्माण भएको विकासको रक्षा गर्ने विषयसँग सरोकार राख्छ।

गत २६ अगस्टमा लङटाङ लिरुङको उच्च भागमा चट्टान र हिमनदीको बरफ फुटेर गयो। यसले भोटेकोशी र त्रिशूली नदीहरूमा पानी, बरफ र लेदोको भीषण बहाव ल्यायो। यस घटनामा १,४०० भन्दा बढी मानिसहरूले ज्यान गुमाए भने ५,००० भन्दा बढी अझै बेपत्ता छन्। बस्ती, सडक, पुल, सीमा नाका र जलविद्युत् आयोजनाहरू ध्वस्त भए। त्यसपछि ११ अक्टोबरमा बुढीगण्डकीमा पहिरोले नदी थुनिएर फुट्दा निर्माणाधीन एक प्रमुख जलविद्युत् आयोजनामा क्षति पुर्यायो।

द्रुत क्षति तथा आवश्यकता आकलन (Rapid Damage and Need Assessment) ले विपद्को कुल प्रभाव करिब २.७ अर्ब अमेरिकी डलर बराबर रहेको र पुनःप्राप्ति तथा पुनर्मार्माणका लागि करिब ४.८ अर्ब डलर आवश्यक पर्ने अनुमान गरेको छ। यी घटनाहरूले हामीले सामना गरिरहेका जोखिमहरूको जटिलतालाई दर्शाउँछन्। सुक्खा हिमपहिरोले नदी थुनेर अस्थायी ताल बनाउन सक्छ र धेरै तल्लो तटीय क्षेत्रमा बाढी ल्याउन सक्छ। केवल वर्षाको पूर्वानुमानले मात्र यो सम्पूर्ण श्रृंखलालाई समेट्न सक्दैन। उच्च हिमालयमा उत्पन्न भएको विपद् केही घण्टामै सयौँ किलोमिटर टाढा, विभिन्न जिल्ला र सीमापारिसम्म पुग्न सक्छ। हाम्रा हिमालहरूको यो नयाँ यथार्थ हो।

जलवायु परिवर्तनले हाम्रो संवेदनशील हिमाली पारिस्थितिकी प्रणालीमा निरन्तर दबाब सिर्जना गरिरहेको छ। प्रत्येक घटनाको विस्तृत वैज्ञानिक अनुसन्धान आवश्यक भए तापनि, अनुगमन र तयारीलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता स्पष्ट छ।

जकार्ता मन्त्रिस्तरीय घोषणापत्रले हाम्रो क्षेत्रलाई एउटा साझा दिशा दिएको छ: मजबुत साझेदारी, डिजिटल प्रविधिको अझ राम्रो प्रयोग, सुधारिएको डाटा व्यवस्थापन, र यी सूचनाहरू प्रयोग गर्ने मानिसहरूसँग नजिकको संलग्नता। भोटेकोशी विपद्को कारण पत्ता लगाउन तत्काल उपग्रहका तस्बिरहरू र प्राविधिक जानकारी उपलब्ध गराएकोमा म ESCAP लाई हार्दिक धन्यवाद दिन्छु। सहायताका लागि म मित्र राष्ट्रहरू, क्षेत्रीय संस्थाहरू र विकास साझेदारहरूलाई पनि धन्यवाद दिन्छु।

ESCAP का प्रतिवेदनहरूमा उल्लेख गरिए अनुसार उपग्रहका तस्बिरहरू र विपद् सम्बन्धी जानकारी साझा गर्ने कार्य, असल अभ्यासहरू, तथा विपद् विश्लेषणका लागि SatGPT प्रयोग गर्ने तालिम सराहनीय छन्। यी उपलब्धिहरूले क्षेत्रीय प्रतिबद्धताहरू कसरी उपयोगी सेवामा परिणत हुन सक्छन् भन्ने देखाउँछन्। अब हामीले यसको पहुँच विस्तार गर्नुपर्छ र यिनको प्रयोगका लागि राष्ट्रिय क्षमता सुदृढ गर्नुपर्छ।

नेपाल यस सम्मेलन समक्ष प्रस्तुत ब्याङ्कक मन्त्रिस्तरीय घोषणापत्रको मस्यौदाको स्वागत गर्दछ। यसले डाटा साझेदारी, अनुकूल प्रणाली, व्यावहारिक डिजिटल उपकरण र प्राविधिक सहायतामा दिएको जोडले सन् २०२६ देखि २०३० सम्मको तेस्रो चरणमा सहयोगलाई सुदृढ बनाउन सक्छ।

सबैका लागि पूर्वसूचना (Early Warnings for All) र दुर्गम तथा हिमाली क्षेत्रमा स्याटेलाइट कनेक्टिभिटीका लागि यसको समर्थन नेपालका लागि विशेष सान्दर्भिक छ। हाम्रा लागि कार्यान्वयनको अर्थ हिमनदी, हिमताल र अस्थिर ढलानहरूको नियमित अनुगमन; माथिल्लो तटीय क्षेत्रका जोखिमबारे समयमै सूचना आदानप्रदान; र समुदायसम्म स्पष्ट मार्गनिर्देशनसहितका चेतावनीहरू पुग्नु हो।

हामी क्षेत्रीय साझेदारहरूलाई उपग्रह अवलोकनलाई जमिनको मापन र स्थानीय ज्ञानसँग संयोजन गर्दै, शृङ्खलाबद्ध (cascading) हिमाली जोखिमहरूमा संयुक्त कार्यक्रमहरू विकास गर्न प्रोत्साहन गर्दछौँ। अन्तरिक्ष अनुप्रयोगहरूले सुरक्षित जलविद्युत् विकास, सिँचाइ आयोजना र जलाधार व्यवस्थापनलाई पनि मार्गदर्शन गर्न सक्छन्।

नेपालको पूर्ण रूपमा स्वच्छ ऊर्जा प्रणालीलाई कायम राख्ने जलविद्युत् विकास, व्यापक ऊर्जा पूर्वाधार र लगानीको सुरक्षा तथा संरक्षण गर्न हामी पूर्ण रूपमा प्रतिबद्ध छौँ।

नेपाल आफ्नो राष्ट्रिय अनुकूलन योजना (२०२१-२०५०), तेस्रो राष्ट्रिय निर्धारित योगदान (NDC), र सन् २०४५ सम्ममा शून्य कार्बन उत्सर्जन (net-zero) हासिल गर्ने लक्ष्यप्रति प्रतिबद्ध छ। विश्वव्यापी हरितगृह ग्यास उत्सर्जनमा हाम्रो नगण्य ०.०१% योगदान भए तापनि, हामी स्वच्छ ऊर्जा, जलवायु उत्थानशीलता र व्यावहारिक क्षेत्रीय सहयोगका लागि प्रतिबद्ध छौँ।

नेपाल बहु-जोखिम र जलवायु परिवर्तनका प्रभावहरू सम्बन्धी अनुसन्धान र सिकाइका लागि क्षेत्रीय केन्द्र (hub) को रूपमा सेवा गर्न तयार छ, साथै एसिया प्रशान्त क्षेत्रभरि बहु-जोखिम जोखिम न्यूनीकरण र व्यवस्थापनमा उत्तम अभ्यासहरू साझा गर्न चाहन्छ।

नेपाल र UN ESCAP ले संयुक्त रूपमा भोलि २९ अक्टोबर बिहान १०:०० बजेदेखि दिउँसो १:०० बजेसम्म सम्मेलन कक्ष ४ मा “सगरमाथादेखि सागरसम्म: एसिया र प्रशान्त क्षेत्रमा शृङ्खलाबद्ध जोखिमहरू विरुद्ध उत्थानशीलता सुदृढ गर्न नेपालको भोटेकोशी-त्रिशूली विपद्का पाठहरू” शीर्षकमा क्षेत्रीय संवाद आयोजना गर्दैछन्। यस कार्यक्रमको उद्देश्य जलवायु, हिमनदी, भू-भौतिकीय र तटीय जोखिमहरू कसरी जोडिन्छन् र “हिमालदेखि समुद्रसम्म” क्षेत्र र सीमापारि विपद्हरू निम्त्याउँछन् भन्ने बुझाइमा सुधार ल्याउनु हो। यसले उपग्रह अवलोकन, भू-स्थानिक विश्लेषण, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (AI) र युवा नेतृत्वको नवप्रवर्तनले विपद् तयारीलाई कसरी सुदृढ बनाउन सक्छ भन्ने कुरालाई उजागर गर्दै डाटा साझेदारी, अनुगमन, पूर्व चेतावनी र जोखिम-सूचित योजनामा क्षेत्रीय सहयोगलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्नेछ।

म सबै प्रतिनिधिमण्डलहरूलाई सहभागी हुन हार्दिक निमन्त्रणा गर्दछु।

आउनुहोस्, ब्याङ्कक घोषणापत्रमार्फत जकार्ताको भावनालाई अगाडि बढाऔँ, जसले देशहरूलाई जोखिम बुझ्न, विकासको रक्षा गर्न र मानिसहरूको जीवन रक्षा गर्न मद्दत गर्नेछ।

Minister Shrestha welcomed the draft of the Bangkok Ministerial Declaration and appealed for strengthening satellite data sharing, early warning systems, and technical cooperation in the third phase from 2026 to 2030. He also reiterated Nepal's commitment to achieving zero carbon emissions by 2045 and protecting a clean energy system, even though Nepal's contribution to greenhouse gas emissions is negligible (0.01%). On the occasion of the conference, he also informed that a regional dialogue on the topic 'From Everest to the Sea: Lessons from the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disaster' will be held on Thursday, October 29, jointly organized by Nepal and the United Nations ESCAP, and requested participation. Despite our negligible contribution of 0.01% to global greenhouse gas emissions, we are committed to clean energy, climate resilience, and practical regional cooperation. Nepal is poised to serve as a regional hub for research and learning on multi-hazards and climate change impacts, as well as share best practices in multi-hazard risk reduction and management across the Asia Pacific region. I cordially invite all delegations to participate. Let us take forward the spirit of Jakarta through the Bangkok Declaration, which will help countries understand risks, protect development, and save lives. Thank you.
